classification: pre-registered recall and geometry parity of the production conjunction screen (screen_catalog, SGP4 on GP) against one full CelesTrak SOCRATES Plus run, on the GP editions SOCRATES used; no truth data; no accuracy claim; Pc is information only

window.basis: the report's TCAs run from 2026-10-28 17:00:08.230 to 2026-11-04 16:59:51.001 UTC; CelesTrak's page states 7 days and 5 km

catalog.cutBasis: the latest CREATION_DATE among editions SOCRATES verifiably used (16:06:35); the earliest it verifiably did not use is 16:46:20

editions.note: 0.0005 d is the rounding of SOCRATES's three-decimal days since epoch; 2e-8 d (1.7 ms) covers the TCA's millisecond text

screen.pairs: every pair with a subset primary: the subset first in catalog order, block b's primaries [p0, p1) against order positions [p0, N), so each pair is screened exactly once; SOCRATES's population is applied in the comparison

primaries.rank: ascending SHA-256 hex of seed + ':' + NORAD_CAT_ID (decimal)
primaries.eligibility: payloads that CelesTrak's SATCAT (fetched 2026-10-29) lists as active, present in the catalog
primaries.order: every eligible primary in rank order, then every other catalog object in catalog order; a block's primaries are order positions [p0, p1) and its secondaries [p0, N), so across both parts each pair with an active primary is screened exactly once

parts.note: reported first; alone it is a subset (36 % of active primaries)
the remaining active primaries, same rules and settings, run straight after Part 1; Parts 1 and 2 together are the whole SOCRATES population

primaries.reason: one 7-day call cannot hold the catalog, and the whole population in one run exceeds the 90-minute budget (PLAN.md, Budget); the population is screened in two registered parts

probe.note: timing probes only, after the registered window; never written to runs/ or results/

comparison.matchRule: same unordered NORAD pair and |TCA difference| <= 60 s, one to one, nearest first (distinct encounters of a fast pair are about half an orbit apart)
comparison.mergeRule: screen events of one pair within 1 s of each other (across a slice boundary or within one) are one encounter

classes.primary: both objects numbered below 100000 and both editions matched (GP on GP)
classes.editionMismatch: both numbered below 100000, an object's edition not matched
classes.numbered100000: an object numbered 100000 or above, reported separately

population.statement: CelesTrak's SOCRATES Plus page: three runs a day screen all active payloads against all objects (analyst 8xxxx and 27xxxx included) over seven days, 5 km, SGP4 in STK 12.2 CAT; operational members of one constellation are not screened against each other; docked objects form one constellation
population.statusSource: the ops status SOCRATES printed in the report for an object it lists; CelesTrak's SATCAT of 2026-10-29 for the others
population.fleetRule: a name prefix with at least 30 operational ([+]) payloads numbered below 100000 in the SATCAT and no report row between two of them both numbered below 100000

comparison.edgeRule: a SOCRATES row or a screen event whose TCA lies within windowEdgeSeconds of either end of the window is counted apart; SOCRATES's never enter a recall denominator

tolerances.pc: information only (SOCRATES's radii are not published)

pass.rule: over Parts 1 and 2 together (every active primary): recall = 1.0 over the primary class (both bands, rows at a window edge apart) and every matched primary-class event within the gated tolerances (NLRV TCA <= 10 ms, miss <= 5 m, speed <= 5 m/s); every miss in any class is a defect listed with its pair, TCA and range; the tail beyond each tolerance is reported per class and stratum with p99 and maximum
pass.fallback: if Part 2 cannot finish, Part 1 is reported alone, labeled as a subset
